### Install and start the Python workbench

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/workbench/python/README.md

```bash
cd workbench/python

WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_MANIFEST=1 pnpm dev
```

--------------------------------

### Framework-agnostic app boundary with start()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/runtime-targets.md

Framework-agnostic app boundary example using plain Request and Response. Starts the onboarding workflow with a userId from the request body and returns the runId.

```ts
import { start } from 'workflow/api';
import { onboardingWorkflow } from '../workflows/onboarding';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const body = (await request.json()) as { userId: string };
  const run = await start(onboardingWorkflow, [body.userId]);
  return Response.json({ runId: run.runId });
}
```

--------------------------------

### Hono app boundary with start()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/runtime-targets.md

Named-framework app boundary example using Hono. Defines a POST route that starts the onboarding workflow and returns the runId as JSON.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { start } from 'workflow/api';
import { onboardingWorkflow } from '../workflows/onboarding';

const app = new Hono();

app.post('/api/onboarding/start', async (c) => {
  const body = (await c.req.json()) as { userId: string };
  const run = await start(onboardingWorkflow, [body.userId]);
  return c.json({ runId: run.runId });
});

export default app;
```

--------------------------------

### Core package testing commands (pnpm test, vitest run, e2e setup)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/AGENTS.md

Commands for testing the core package. Includes running unit tests, targeting a specific test file, and the full local E2E workflow: start the dev server with WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_MANIFEST=1, wait, run the E2E test with required environment variables, and stop the server. Use nextjs-turbopack for local E2E testing because the example app has no dev server.

```bash
# Test core functionality
cd packages/core && pnpm test

# Test specific file
cd packages/core && pnpm vitest run src/[filename].test.ts

# Run E2E tests (requires environment variables and running dev server)
# Note: Use nextjs-turbopack for local e2e testing (not example app - it has no dev server)

# Step 1: Start the dev server in background
# NOTE: WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_MANIFEST=1 is required for e2e tests to access the workflow manifest
cd workbench/nextjs-turbopack && WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_MANIFEST=1 pnpm dev > /tmp/nextjs-dev.log 2>&1 &

# Step 2: Wait for server to be ready (usually 15-20 seconds)
sleep 15

# Step 3: Run the e2e tests from the project root
DEPLOYMENT_URL="http://localhost:3000" APP_NAME="nextjs-turbopack" pnpm vitest run packages/core/e2e/e2e.test.ts

# Step 4: Stop the dev server when done
pkill -f "pnpm dev"

# To run specific tests, use the -t flag:
DEPLOYMENT_URL="http://localhost:3000" APP_NAME="nextjs-turbopack" pnpm vitest run packages/core/e2e/e2e.test.ts -t "sleeping"
```

### Start Postgres World in SvelteKit hooks.server.ts

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

Creates a src/hooks.server.ts file with a ServerInit hook that starts the World's background worker on server initialization.

```ts
import type { ServerInit } from "@sveltejs/kit";

export const init: ServerInit = async () => {
  const { getWorld } = await import("workflow/runtime");
  const world = await getWorld();
  await world.start?.();
};
```

### Run E2E tests against deployed Vercel app (environment variables example)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/AGENTS.md

Command to run E2E tests locally against a deployed Vercel preview/production app. Requires many environment variables (DEPLOYMENT_URL, VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID, APP_NAME, WORKFLOW_VERCEL_ENV, WORKFLOW_VERCEL_AUTH_TOKEN, WORKFLOW_VERCEL_TEAM, WORKFLOW_VERCEL_PROJECT, WORKFLOW_VERCEL_PROJECT_SLUG, VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN). The example uses a nextjs-turbopack preview deployment and pulls VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN from the workbench app's .env.local.

```bash
NODE_OPTIONS="--enable-source-maps" \
DEPLOYMENT_URL="https://example-nextjs-workflow-turbopack-<hash>.labs.vercel.dev" \
VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID="dpl_..." \
APP_NAME="nextjs-turbopack" \
WORKFLOW_VERCEL_ENV="preview" \
WORKFLOW_VERCEL_AUTH_TOKEN="<vercel_labs_token>" \
WORKFLOW_VERCEL_TEAM="team_nO2mCG4W8IxPIeKoSsqwAxxB" \
WORKFLOW_VERCEL_PROJECT="prj_yjkM7UdHliv8bfxZ1sMJQf1pMpdi" \
WORKFLOW_VERCEL_PROJECT_SLUG="example-nextjs-workflow-turbopack" \
VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN="$(grep VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN workbench/nextjs-turbopack/.env.local | cut -d= -f2-)" \
pnpm run test:e2e
```

### Start Postgres World in Next.js instrumentation.ts

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

Creates an instrumentation.ts file to start the World's background worker on server boot. Skips edge runtime and calls world.start?.() after importing workflow/runtime.

```ts
export async function register() {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME !== "edge") {
    const { getWorld } = await import("workflow/runtime");
    const world = await getWorld();
    await world.start?.();
  }
}
```

### WorkflowAgent example with tool and streaming

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Shows how to create a durable agent with WorkflowAgent, define a step-backed tool, stream model-call output, and limit model calls with stopWhen. The example uses the default model spacexai/grok-4.6 and a plain provider/model string routed through Vercel AI Gateway.

```typescript
import { WorkflowAgent, type ModelCallStreamPart } from "@ai-sdk/workflow";
import { isStepCount, tool } from "ai";
import { getWritable } from "workflow";
import { z } from "zod";

async function lookupData({ query }: { query: string }) {
  "use step";
  // Step functions have full Node.js access
  return `Results for "${query}"`;
}

export async function myAgentWorkflow(userMessage: string) {
  "use workflow";

  const agent = new WorkflowAgent({
    model: "spacexai/grok-4.6",
    instructions: "You are a helpful assistant.",
    tools: {
      lookupData: tool({
        description: "Search for information",
        inputSchema: z.object({ query: z.string() }),
        execute: lookupData,
      }),
    },
  });

  const result = await agent.stream({
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: userMessage }],
    writable: getWritable<ModelCallStreamPart>(),
    stopWhen: isStepCount(10),
  });

  return result.messages;
}
```

### Create workflow file with directives

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Create workflow files in src/ with 'use workflow' and 'use step' directives. The example shows a step function and a workflow function that calls it.

```typescript
// src/workflows/example.ts
export async function myStep(data: string) {
  'use step';
  return data.toUpperCase();
}

export async function myWorkflow(input: string) {
  'use workflow';
  const result = await myStep(input);
  return result;
}
```

### Start Postgres World in Nitro plugin

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

```ts
import { defineNitroPlugin } from "nitro/~internal/runtime/plugin";

export default defineNitroPlugin(async () => {
  const { getWorld } = await import("workflow/runtime");
  const world = await getWorld();
  await world.start?.();
});
```

### Startup helper for Workflow SDK runtime

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/evals/non-vercel-runtime-branch.md

A helper function that starts the workflow world by calling getWorld().start?.(). Use this at the app boundary to initialize the runtime. It is framework-agnostic and does not rely on Next.js-specific route syntax.

```TypeScript
import { getWorld } from 'workflow/runtime';

export async function startWorkflowWorld(): Promise<void> {
  await getWorld().start?.();
}
```

### Child workflow via step-wrapped start/getRun

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/shared-patterns.md

Shows how to spawn and collect a child workflow using step-wrapped functions. start launches the child and returns a runId; getRun retrieves the run and its return value. The child workflow and step functions are defined in the same file.

```TypeScript
import { getRun, start } from 'workflow/api';

export async function childWorkflow(input: string) {
  'use workflow';
  return await doWork(input);
}

async function doWork(input: string) {
  'use step';
  return { input, status: 'done' as const };
}

async function spawnChild(input: string): Promise<string> {
  'use step';
  const run = await start(childWorkflow, [input]);
  return run.runId;
}

async function collectChild(runId: string) {
  'use step';
  const run = getRun(runId);
  return (await run.returnValue) as { input: string; status: 'done' };
}
```

--------------------------------

### CLI: build

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Builds workflow bundles for local development. Use --vercel to emit a Vercel Build Output API directory.

```APIDOC
## CLI: build

### Description
Builds workflow bundles for local development. Use --vercel to emit a Vercel Build Output API directory.

### Method
build

### Parameters
#### Options
- **--vercel** (boolean) - Optional - Emit a Vercel Build Output API directory (`.vercel/output`) with the workflow queue-consumer function. Implied when the `VERCEL` env var is set. Default: off (on under `VERCEL`).
- **--dirs** (string) - Optional - Comma-separated workflow source directories to scan. Default: `src`.
- **--entry** (string) - Optional - Vercel app entry module that default-exports a Node request handler. Auto-detected (e.g. `_vercel/entry.js`).
- **--out-dir** (string) - Optional - Output directory for local-dev bundles (ignored with `--vercel`). Default: `.nestjs/workflow`.
- **--module** (string) - Optional - SWC module type: `es6` or `commonjs`. Default: `es6`.
- **--base-path** (string) - Optional - Route prefix the app is served under. Must match `setGlobalPrefix()` / `basePath`. Default: none.
- **--sourcemap** (string) - Optional - esbuild sourcemap mode: `true`, `false`, `inline`, `linked`, `external`, `both`. Default: builder default.
- **--max-duration** (number) - Optional - `maxDuration` for the app function. Default: `300`.
- **--runtime** (string) - Optional - Vercel runtime for the emitted functions, e.g. `nodejs22.x`. Default: platform default.
- **--app-function** (string) - Optional - Name of the catch-all app function. Default: `__nest`.
- **--external** (string) - Optional - Comma-separated packages to leave as bare `require()` calls instead of bundling, for dependencies resolved at runtime behind `try`/`catch`. Vercel builds only. Default: none.

### Request Example
```bash
# Build workflow bundles for local dev
npx @workflow/nest build

# Emit the Vercel Build Output (.vercel/output); implied when VERCEL is set
npx @workflow/nest build --vercel
```
```

--------------------------------

### Deterministic server-side resume with createHook and resumeHook

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/shared-patterns.md

Deterministic server-side resume example. The workflow uses `createHook()` with a token, and the POST handler calls `resumeHook()` with the same token pattern. This is the non-Hono variant that uses plain `Request`/`Response`.

```ts
import { createHook } from 'workflow';
import { resumeHook } from 'workflow/api';

export async function approvalWorkflow(orderId: string) {
  'use workflow';

  using approval = createHook<{ approved: boolean }>({
    token: `order:${orderId}:approval`,
  });

  return await approval;
}

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const body = (await request.json()) as {
    orderId: string;
    approved: boolean;
  };

  await resumeHook(`order:${body.orderId}:approval`, {
    approved: body.approved,
  });

  return Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```

### Expected excerpt using createWebhook()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/evals/callback-url-default-response.md

Expected SDK code that creates a webhook, sends a verification request with the webhook URL, and awaits the request to get the payload.

```ts
using verification = createWebhook();
await sendVerificationRequest(documentId, verification.url);
const request = await verification;
const payload = await request.json();
```

### Self-hosted World interface and startup

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/aws-step-functions.md

Self-hosted runtime requirements: a World interface extending Queue, Streamer, and Storage with an optional start method, and a startup function that calls getWorld().start?.() to run background workers. Required for self-hosted deployments.

```ts
interface World extends Queue, Streamer, Storage {
  start?(): Promise<void>;
}
```

```ts
import { getWorld } from 'workflow/runtime';

export async function startWorkflowWorld(): Promise<void> {
  await getWorld().start?.();
}
```

### Add pre-build scripts to package.json

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Add a prebuild script that runs the init command with --force to regenerate configuration before builds, and a build script that runs nest build.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "prebuild": "npx @workflow/nest init --force",
    "build": "nest build"
  }
}
```

### Bootstrap database with CLI (npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/world-postgres/README.md

Run the bootstrap command to set up the database. The CLI loads the connection string from WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL, then DATABASE_URL, then defaults to postgres://world:world@localhost:5432/world. Requires PostgreSQL access and permissions to create tables and manage jobs.

```bash
# npm
npx --package=@workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
```

```bash
# pnpm
pnpm dlx --package @workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
```

```bash
# Yarn
yarn dlx --package @workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
```

```bash
# Bun
bunx --package @workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
```

### CLI commands for @workflow/nest

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Commands to initialize SWC configuration, build workflow bundles, emit Vercel Build Output, and show help. Use --force to overwrite existing config; --vercel is implied when VERCEL is set.

```Bash
# Generate .swcrc configuration
npx @workflow/nest init

# Force regenerate (overwrites existing)
npx @workflow/nest init --force

# Build workflow bundles for local dev
npx @workflow/nest build

# Emit the Vercel Build Output (.vercel/output); implied when VERCEL is set
npx @workflow/nest build --vercel

# Show help
npx @workflow/nest --help
```

# `vercel inspect` prints the dpl_... ID for a deployment URL

### Set up Vercel World in a script

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/vercel.mdx

Use this script to configure the Vercel World with explicit credentials before starting a workflow. Requires the token, project ID, and team ID to be set together.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";
import { setWorld } from "workflow/runtime";
import { createWorld } from "@workflow/world-vercel";
import { myWorkflow } from "../workflows/my-workflow";

setWorld(
  createWorld({
    token: process.env.WORKFLOW_VERCEL_AUTH_TOKEN, // [!code highlight]
    projectConfig: {
      projectId: process.env.WORKFLOW_VERCEL_PROJECT, // [!code highlight]
      teamId: process.env.WORKFLOW_VERCEL_TEAM, // [!code highlight]
      environment: process.env.WORKFLOW_VERCEL_ENV, // [!code highlight]
    },
  })
);

const run = await start(myWorkflow, ["input"]);
console.log(run.runId);
```

### Set up conformance test suite with createTestSuite

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-world-v4-to-v5/SKILL.md

Wire up the conformance suite before migration verification. The suite spawns a server with WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD set to the given value and runs real workflows against it. Requires a built entrypoint that plain node can load and whose createWorld() works with no arguments.

```typescript
import { createTestSuite } from '@workflow/world-testing';

createTestSuite('@my-org/my-world'); // or a path to the built entrypoint
```

### FastifyAdapter with bodyLimit

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Raise Fastify's body limit on the adapter because it is per instance and cannot be scoped to workflow routes. The default is 1 MiB, and WorkflowModule logs a warning at startup if it is not raised.

```typescript
const app = await NestFactory.create(
  AppModule,
  new FastifyAdapter({ bodyLimit: 16 * 1024 * 1024 })
);
```

### Claude statusline configuration in settings.json

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/internal-dev-workbench/SKILL.md

Wire the statusline helper into ~/.claude/settings.json so it runs across all sessions and worktrees. Point the command path at your primary checkout, not a worktree, because worktrees get deleted and break the path. The script reads Claude's workspace.current from stdin to derive the current branch.

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "$HOME/github/vercel/workflow/skills/internal-dev-workbench/statusline.sh"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Instance method step: input class with custom serialization

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/swc-plugin-workflow/spec.md

Input example of an instance method using `"use step"`. The class provides custom serialization methods `WORKFLOW_SERIALIZE` and `WORKFLOW_DESERIALIZE` from `@workflow/serde`.

```javascript
import { WORKFLOW_SERIALIZE, WORKFLOW_DESERIALIZE } from '@workflow/serde';

export class Counter {
  static [WORKFLOW_SERIALIZE](instance) {
    return { value: instance.value };
  }
  static [WORKFLOW_DESERIALIZE](data) {
    return new Counter(data.value);
  }
  constructor(value) {
    this.value = value;
  }
  async add(amount) {
    'use step';
    return this.value + amount;
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Start a workflow from an API route

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Use start() from an API route to launch a workflow. The function returns a run object with a runId. For a no-arg workflow, call start(noArgWorkflow) without arguments.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";

// From an API route; works directly
export async function POST() {
  const run = await start(myWorkflow, [arg1, arg2]);
  return Response.json({ runId: run.runId });
}

// No-args workflow
const run = await start(noArgWorkflow);
```

### Start world in Next.js instrumentation.ts

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/world-postgres/HOW_IT_WORKS.md

Add this to instrumentation.ts|js to start graphile-worker workers before request handling in Next.js. It imports getWorld from workflow/runtime and calls world.start() only when not on the edge runtime.

```TypeScript
// instrumentation.ts

if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME !== "edge") {
  import("workflow/runtime").then(async ({ getWorld }) => {
    // start listening to the jobs.
    const world = await getWorld();
    await world.start?.();
  });
}
```

### world.steps.list()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Lists steps for a given run with pagination and optional data resolution.

```APIDOC
## world.steps.list()

### Description
Lists steps for a given run with pagination and optional data resolution.

### Method
N/A (SDK method)

### Endpoint
N/A

### Parameters
#### Query Parameters
- **runId** (string) - Required - The ID of the run (top-level, not inside pagination).
- **pagination** (object) - Optional - Pagination object with nested cursor: `{ pagination: { cursor } }`.
- **resolveData** (string) - Optional - 'all' (default) or 'none' to include or exclude I/O data.

### Request Example
```typescript
const { data, cursor } = await world.steps.list({ runId, pagination: { cursor }, resolveData: 'all' | 'none' });
```

### Response
#### Success Response
- **data** (array) - List of steps.
- **cursor** (string) - Pagination cursor for next page.

#### Response Example
```typescript
const { data, cursor } = await world.steps.list({ runId, pagination: { cursor }, resolveData: 'all' });
```
```

### Start a child workflow from inside a workflow

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Call start() from within a workflow function to spawn a child run. The child run is created without waiting for it to complete; use childRun.returnValue only when the parent should wait.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";

export async function parentWorkflow() {
  "use workflow";
  const childRun = await start(childWorkflow, ["some data"]);
  await sleep("1h");
  return { childRunId: childRun.runId };
}
```

--------------------------------

### Hono app boundary for starting refund workflow

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/aws-step-functions.md

Hono app boundary that exposes a POST /api/refunds/start endpoint, parses the refundId from the request body, starts the refundWorkflow with that ID, and returns the runId in the JSON response.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { start } from 'workflow/api';
import { refundWorkflow } from '../workflows/refund';

const app = new Hono();

app.post('/api/refunds/start', async (c) => {
  const body = (await c.req.json()) as { refundId: string };
  const run = await start(refundWorkflow, [body.refundId]);
  return c.json({ runId: run.runId });
});

export default app;
```

### Explicit region selection with start()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/vercel.mdx

Pass the `region` option to `start()` to pin a run to a specific Vercel Function region. The region controls data storage and queue dispatch, but does not deploy your code; your app must be deployed there for execution to occur in that region.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";
import { myWorkflow } from "@/workflows/my-workflow";

const run = await start(myWorkflow, [input], { region: "sfo1" });
```

### Same-named steps in different block scopes - step mode output

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/swc-plugin-workflow/spec.md

Step mode output for the two `act` steps. The first is hoisted as `example$act` with step ID `step//./input//example/act`; the second as `example$act$1` with step ID `step//./input//example/act~1`. Registration IIFEs are abbreviated.

```javascript
var example$act = async ()=>
"a";
(function(__wf_fn, __wf_id) { /* ... */ })(example$act, "step//./input//example/act");
var example$act$1 = async ()=>
"b";
(function(__wf_fn, __wf_id) { /* ... */ })(example$act$1, "step//./input//example/act~1");
```

### Inspect workflows and launch web UI with Workflow CLI

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

```bash
# Set your database URL

# List workflow runs
npx workflow inspect runs --backend @workflow/world-postgres

# Launch the web UI
npx workflow web --backend @workflow/world-postgres
```

### WorkflowModule.forRoot()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Initializes the WorkflowModule with optional configuration options. Use this method to configure the module for your NestJS application.

```APIDOC
## WorkflowModule.forRoot()

### Description
Initializes the WorkflowModule with optional configuration options.

### Method
forRoot

### Parameters
#### Options
- **dirs** (string[]) - Optional - Workflow source directories to scan.
- **outDir** (string) - Optional - Output directory for local-dev bundles.
- **skipBuild** (boolean) - Optional - Only with `workflow-nest build` in your build step: startup fails fast if the bundles are missing. Defaults to true on Vercel, where they always are.
- **moduleType** (string) - Optional - SWC module type: `commonjs` if using SWC CommonJS compilation.
- **distDir** (string) - Optional - Where compiled .js files live.

### Request Example
```ts
import { WorkflowModule } from '@workflow/nest';

// Basic usage
WorkflowModule.forRoot()

// With options
WorkflowModule.forRoot({
  dirs: ['src/workflows'],
  outDir: '.nestjs/workflow',
  // Only with `workflow-nest build` in your build step: startup fails fast if
  // the bundles are missing. Defaults to true on Vercel, where they always are.
  skipBuild: true,
  moduleType: 'commonjs',  // if using SWC CommonJS compilation
  distDir: 'dist',          // where compiled .js files live
})
```
```

--------------------------------

### Configure PostgreSQL world with environment variables

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/world-postgres/README.md

Set required and optional environment variables for the PostgreSQL world. Defaults are noted for optional settings.

```bash
# Required: PostgreSQL connection string
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://username:password@localhost:5432/database"

# Optional: Job prefix for queue operations
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_JOB_PREFIX="myapp"

# Optional: Worker concurrency (default: 10)
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_WORKER_CONCURRENCY="10"

# Optional: Internal pg.Pool max size (default: 10)
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_MAX_POOL_SIZE="10"

# Optional: Let the application coordinate shutdown (default: false)
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_APPLICATION_MANAGED_SHUTDOWN="1"

# Optional: Maximum Hook minimum retention in days (default: 30)
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_HOOK_RETENTION_LIMIT_DAYS="30"

# Optional: Seconds a running delivery's job lock may go unrenewed before
# another process redelivers the job (default: 0, off; 30 is a good value
# when more than one process shares the database, see "Crash recovery")
export WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_JOB_LOCK_STALE_SECONDS="30"
```

### Configure nest-cli.json to use SWC builder

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Set the builder to 'swc' in nest-cli.json so NestJS uses SWC for compilation.

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "builder": "swc"
  }

### experimental_setAttributes renamed to setAttributes

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-workflow-v4-to-v5/SKILL.md

The experimental_setAttributes export was renamed to setAttributes in v5. Update imports accordingly. The options type is now SetAttributesOptions, and the attributes option on start() is unchanged.

```typescript
// v4
import { experimental_setAttributes } from 'workflow';

// v5
import { setAttributes } from 'workflow';
```

### Inspect runs and runs with CLI

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

```bash
# CLI inspection (use --json for machine-readable output, --help for full usage)
npx workflow inspect runs
npx workflow inspect run <run_id>

# For Vercel-deployed projects, specify backend and project
npx workflow inspect runs --backend vercel --project <project-name> --team <team-slug>
npx workflow inspect run <run_id> --backend vercel --project <project-name> --team <team-slug>
